SPECIFIC D0 DIRECTIVE — PUBLISHED-CLASS LIFT AND ORDERED-RANK SHARPENING.

Class finding: the note does not use the published Arkhangelsky–Imbens–Lei–Luo class. Their Theorem 4.1 allows arbitrary binary-path support, non-i.i.d. and weakly dependent units, unit-specific known propensities conditional on the full potential-outcome schedule, Assumptions 2.1–2.3, and unit-specific effects. The note instead assumes absorbing paths, an i.i.d. superpopulation, a common propensity conditional on X, and pathwise mean ignorability. These classes are incomparable overall, while the note is strictly narrower in path and sampling structure. Thus the present achievability claim does not transfer by inclusion and thm:homogeneous-strict-extension does not literally “reproduce Theorem 4.1”; it only reproduces its coefficient algebra in a different subclass. Published theorem and hypotheses: https://www.econometricsociety.org/publications/quantitative-economics/2024/11/01/Design-Robust-Two-Way-Fixed-Effects-Regression-For-Panel-Data/file/quan200345.pdf

Targets: def:model-class, lem:support-rank, thm:calendar-lag-loading, thm:homogeneous-strict-extension, prop:exact-forward-diagnostic, and thm:adjacent-ratio-determinant-sign-rule.

Exact mathematical change:

1. Split the design algebra from the causal sampling layer. Let the base support be any finite S subset of {0,1}^T. The pair-mass identities, support-only kernel, normalization, and rational forward diagnostic already prove unchanged on this larger class. Define C_Pi(u,v)=Cov_Pi(W_u,W_v) and state the displayed G and h formulas with C_Pi; recover C_Pi=K_Pi only as the absorbing-path corollary.

2. Add an anchor-faithful estimator corollary: under the published unit-indexed known-propensity setup and Assumptions 2.1–2.3, but with E[Y_it(w)]=mu_it+sum_{ell=0}^p tau_{i,t,ell} w_{t-ell} and bar_tau_{t,ell,n}=n^{-1}sum_i tau_{i,t,ell}, prove hat_tau_ex - sum_{t=1}^T sum_{ell=0}^p L_{.,t,ell}(Pi) bar_tau_{t,ell,n}=o_P(1). Calendar homogeneity then gives exactly hat_tau_{-ell}=n^{-1}sum_i tau_{i,-ell}+o_P(1), genuinely recovering published Theorem 4.1. The existing three-period counterexample can be embedded in this class using randomized assignment, so its nonreduction conclusion transfers upward.

3. Sharpen lem:support-rank on absorbing supports to a combinatorial criterion. On vertices {bottom,0,...,p}, connect t-u_a and t-u_b for every t=2,...,T when both lie in [0,p], and connect the in-range vertex to bottom when exactly one does. Then dim ker G(Pi) equals the number of graph components not containing bottom, so full rank is equivalent to every lag vertex being connected to bottom. This follows by first-differencing D_uv, since J E_ab v=0 iff v_{t-u_a}=v_{t-u_b} for all t>=2. This is a genuinely ordered, support-only classification rather than a matrix computation.

4. Recast thm:adjacent-ratio-determinant-sign-rule as a pointwise Cramer determinant certificate unless a true global chamber classification is supplied. Its present proof is only L=adj(Gamma)g/det(Gamma); it does not solve the advertised structural sign frontier. Remove def:ordered-sign-handle’s unused LDL^T/Cauchy–Binet claim and fix the malformed 0,ldots,p ranges.

Required prose synchronization: update the TL;DR, Gap/Fill, related work, comparator table, sampling model, and Honest scope to distinguish the arbitrary-path algebra, published-class statistical corollary, absorbing ordered corollaries, and the still-open global sign-chamber problem. Remove the current contradiction in which the final theorem claims a complete rule while the TL;DR and Honest scope call that rule unresolved.

CLOSE/REDERIVE CORRECTION FOR PR 54347e947bb9.

Two defects block a faithful merge:

1. The proposed lem:absorbing-graph-rank is missing positivity in its first conclusion. As written, dim ker G(Pi) equals the graph component count for an unrestricted Pi in Delta(S), which is false on the boundary. Counterexample: T=2, p=0, S={00,01}; the graph connects lag vertex 0 to bottom, but Pi_00=1 and Pi_01=0 gives G(Pi)=0 with one-dimensional kernel. State the equality for every positive law on S, equivalently under the reshaping floor. In the proof, order the paths by adoption date before using the interval formula, or use the signed step-function difference directly. The graph criterion is otherwise correct.

2. The proposed def:published-ripw-dynamic-estimator omits the grand intercept mu from the weighted least-squares problem, although Arkhangelsky–Imbens–Lei–Luo equation (4.2) includes it. With both sum_i alpha_i=0 and sum_t lambda_t=0, that intercept is not redundant. Counterexample: T=2, p=0, S={00,01}, Pi=(1/2,1/2), i.i.d. assignment, and constant potential outcomes Y_it(w)=1 with all treatment effects zero. These satisfy the stated conditions, but the no-intercept regression coefficient converges to 2 rather than zero. Add mu in R and the term mu 1_T exactly as in equation (4.2). Also define the RIP weight as zero off S to avoid an unstated 0/0 convention. Rederive thm:published-class-calendar-loading and its meta claim after correcting the estimator.

The REVIEW assume-the-crux warning on thm:adjacent-ratio-determinant-sign-rule is a false positive. The premise ker H_S={0} already appeared in the base theorem, is ordinary invertibility, and does not assume any determinant sign or zero conclusion. Retain the revised theorem as a fixed-law Cramer certificate and explicitly leave global sign chambers open.

Do not claim a CLT or asymptotic normality.

If c*>0, a rational isolating interval with positive lower endpoint plus the universal bound is a metric separation certificate; do not claim a linear separating hyperplane.
